s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive visual disturbance and endocrine dysfunction due to a large sellar/suprasellar mass
salient_findings: Large sellar/suprasellar mass with heterogeneous signal on MRI
key_facts: Bilateral decrease in visual acuity, worse on the left
Large sellar/suprasellar mass on CT and MRI
Mass extends into both cavernous sinuses and has bony remodeling of the sella turcica and upper clivus
Heterogeneous low T1 signal and intermediate high T2 signal on MRI
Mild patchy postcontrast enhancement on MRI

shortlist.label: Pituitary macroadenoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large sellar/suprasellar mass with bony remodeling and heterogeneous signal on MRI, consistent with a macroadenoma

shortlist.label: Craniopharyngioma
shortlist.why_kept: Sellar/suprasellar mass with calcifications and cystic components, although less likely given the patient's age and lack of calcifications on imaging

shortlist.label: Meningioma
shortlist.why_kept: Dural-based mass with bony remodeling and heterogeneous enhancement, although less likely given the location and signal characteristics

shortlist.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammatory condition that can cause a sellar/suprasellar mass and endocrine dysfunction, although less likely given the size and signal characteristics of the mass

shortlist.label: Pituitary carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive pituitary tumor that can cause a large sellar/suprasellar mass and metastasis, although rare and less likely given the lack of metastatic disease on imaging

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms and imaging findings are consistent with a large pituitary macroadenoma, including bitemporal headache, progressive diminution of vision, and a large sellar/suprasellar mass on CT and MRI. The presence of central hypothyroidism also supports this diagnosis, as pituitary macroadenomas can compress the pituitary gland and stalk, leading to hormonal deficiencies.

rejected.label: Craniopharyngioma
rejected.why: Typically presents with calcifications on imaging, which are not mentioned in the case

rejected.label: Meningioma
rejected.why: Usually has a more homogeneous appearance on MRI and may have a dural tail, which is not described

rejected.label: Lymphocytic hypophysitis
rejected.why: Typically presents with a more acute onset of symptoms and may have a more inflammatory appearance on imaging

rejected.label: Pituitary carcinoma
rejected.why: Is a rare and aggressive tumor that would likely have more rapid progression of symptoms and metastatic disease, which is not described in the case
